query: Consult and cite the primary Standard Webhooks specification at https://github.com/standard-webhooks/standard-webhooks/blob/main/spec/standard-webhooks.md and OWASP SSRF Prevention Cheat Sheet. In at most 700 words answer ONLY: exact signed bytes and base64 whsec_ decoding, multi-signature rotation, timestamp window; HTTPS redirect rejection, resolve ALL IPv4/IPv6 addresses and pin validated IP at actual connection to prevent DNS rebinding. State which parts are specification versus operational local policy. Include full source URLs.

content.text:
For Standard Webhooks, verify the signature over the exact bytes received on the HTTP body, not parsed/re-serialized JSON. For outbound delivery, treat destination validation, redirect handling, and DNS-rebinding defenses as operational security policy rather than requirements of the signing specification.

## Standard Webhooks specification

- Exact signed bytes. Construct the signed message as the byte concatenation of:textwebhook-id + "." + webhook-timestamp + "." + raw HTTP request-body bytesThat is msg_id.timestamp.payload. The payload is precisely the body as transmitted—whitespace, key order, Unicode encoding, line endings, and escaping must remain unchanged. Do not parse JSON before verification and serialize it again; even one altered space invalidates the cryptographic result.
```
webhook-id + "." + webhook-timestamp + "." + raw HTTP request-body bytes
```
- whsec_ decoding. For symmetric signing, the supplied signing secret is serialized as whsec_ followed by a Base64-encoded key. Remove only the literal whsec_ prefix, Base64-decode the remainder into raw key bytes, then compute HMAC-SHA-256 over the exact signed bytes above. A symmetric signature has the form v1,<base64-signature>. This serialization and v1 algorithm identifier are part of the Standard Webhooks specification.
- Multi-signature rotation. webhook-signature is a space-delimited list, not a single value. During zero-downtime rotation, the sender signs the same canonical byte sequence with both current and previous keys and includes both values, for example:textwebhook-signature: v1,<current-base64> v1,<previous-base64>The receiver should attempt each supported signature against each currently trusted verification key and accept if at least one validates; use constant-time comparison for HMAC results. The multiple-signature format and rotation purpose are specification; key-retention duration, maximum signatures/keys, telemetry, and retirement schedule are local policy.
```
webhook-signature: v1,<current-base64> v1,<previous-base64>
```
- Timestamp window. webhook-timestamp is an integer Unix timestamp in seconds and is part of the signed input. The specification requires checking it is within “some allowable tolerance” of current time to mitigate replay, but does not prescribe a numeric window. A 300-second past/future skew allowance, clock-skew monitoring, and rejecting malformed/negative/far-future timestamps are operational local policy. Separately, persist webhook-id as an idempotency key to prevent duplicate processing.

## SSRF delivery policy

- Reject redirects. Configure the outbound HTTP client with redirects disabled. Treat every 3xx as failed delivery; do not fetch the Location target. Standard Webhooks recommends treating 3xx as failure rather than following redirects, while OWASP explicitly says disabling redirect following prevents validation bypass. Thus, redirect rejection is a strong operational policy, aligned with both sources, rather than a cryptographic-signature requirement.
- Resolve all addresses. For a customer-controlled hostname, resolve both DNS A and AAAA records. Validate every returned IPv4 and IPv6 address before any connection: reject loopback, unspecified, link-local, private/internal, multicast, reserved/special-use, metadata-service, and any organization-specific prohibited network ranges. Do not accept a hostname merely because one answer is public while another is internal. OWASP specifically calls for retrieving all A and AAAA addresses to counter DNS pinning and validating their public status.
- Pin the validated address at connect time. DNS validation alone has a time-of-check/time-of-use gap: the HTTP stack may resolve the hostname again and connect to a rebinding-controlled address. Resolve once through a controlled resolver, validate the complete answer set, select one allowed address, then make the actual TCP/TLS connection to that numeric IP—not a later hostname lookup—while preserving the original hostname only for TLS SNI and certificate hostname verification. Reject if the client cannot guarantee this binding; do not permit automatic retry/re-resolution to an unvalidated address. This connection pinning detail is operational local policy derived from OWASP’s DNS-pinning threat model; it is not stated as a Standard Webhooks protocol requirement. Defense in depth should also enforce egress filtering/proxy controls so workers cannot reach internal networks.

## Sources

- Standard Webhooks specification: https://github.com/standard-webhooks/standard-webhooks/blob/main/spec/standard-webhooks.md
- OWASP SSRF Prevention Cheat Sheet: https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Server_Side_Request_Forgery_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html
